definition: A mental set is the current pattern or approach the mind uses to guide thinking and behavior. Shifting mental set means changing that approach when circumstances change, so reduced ability to do this reflects cognitive inflexibility.

reasons: The packet does not define “mental set” as “the current pattern or approach the mind uses to guide thinking and behavior”; it only mentions “shift mental set” in relation to cognitive inflexibility.

The claim that “Shifting mental set means changing that approach when circumstances change” is only partially supported (the packet links mental-set shifting to cognitive inflexibility with changing circumstances, but does not provide the specific explanatory wording about “approach the mind uses”).
“Reduced ability to do this reflects cognitive inflexibility” is supported by the packet (cognitive inflexibility is described as reduced capacity to shift mental set/update behavior).

The packet supports mental set only in the phrase “shift mental set or update behavior when circumstances change”; it does not support defining mental set as a “current pattern or approach the mind uses to guide thinking and behavior.”
The definition adds an explanatory gloss about what shifting mental set means that is broader than the source packet and is not directly supported there.
